extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, Scientific Review Officers, and NIH IC staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for initial and advisory peer review of NIH research grant and cooperative agreement applications, including the review criteria, scoring system, reviewer/SRO duties, summary statements, appeals, and post-review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria, and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall impact score is based on consideration of Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment, and applicable additional criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Scored review criterion: Significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates importance of the problem or critical barrier to progress in the field that the project addresses (implicit from NIH rubric). Reviewers assign a numerical score for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scored review criterion: Investigator(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the qualifications, experience, and suitability of the project personnel; reviewers assign a numerical score for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scored review criterion: Innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether the application challenges and seeks to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms; reviewers assign a numerical score for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Scored review criterion: Approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the strategy, methodology, and analyses proposed and whether they are well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the aims; reviewers assign a numerical score for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Scored review criterion: Environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources that contribute to the probability of success; reviewers assign a numerical score for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Timeline (clinical trials specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criterion specific to applications involving clinical trials: Study Timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered while determining scientific and technical merit and in providing an overall impact score, but no separate score is given for this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criterion: Protections for Human Subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated as applicable; impacts determination of scientific and technical merit and overall impact, but not given a separate numeric score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criterion: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed as applicable to the project; considered in the overall impact determination without separate numeric scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criterion: Vertebrate Animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated as applicable; reviewers consider welfare and appropriateness, included in overall impact assessment but not separately scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criterion: Biohazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed when relevant; considered in overall impact but not scored separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criterion: Resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers consider resubmission characteristics as part of overall merit but do not assign a separate score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criterion: Renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed as applicable to renewals; considered in overall impact without separate scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criterion: Revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated when relevant; contributes to overall impact judgements but not separately scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations (consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review consideration: Applications from Foreign Organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider this item where applicable, but it is not given a score and should not be used in providing the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent (consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review consideration: Select Agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered when applicable; not scored and should not be included in overall impact scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review consideration: Resource Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider resource sharing plans (e.g., data sharing) but do not give separate scores and should not factor them into the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review consideration: Authentication of key resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed as applicable; considered but not scored separately and should not be used in overall impact scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support (consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review consideration: Budget and Period Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider appropriateness of budget and period of support when relevant; this is not separately scored and should not be used to determine the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH 9-point scoring scale and scoring process
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH utilizes a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for all applications; the same scale is used for overall impact scores and for criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the SRG meeting, each assigned reviewer gives a separate score for each of (at least) five review criteria and a preliminary overall impact score. For discussed applications, each eligible committee member gives a final impact score; the final overall impact score is the mean of eligible members' final impact scores multiplied by 10, producing a range of 10 (high impact) through 90 (low impact). Applications not discussed are reported as ND (may be shown as ++).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement content and percentile reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements report written comments and scores from assigned reviewers and discussants for each scored review criterion; percentiles indicate the approximate percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentiles are reported as whole numbers; only a subset of applications receive percentiles; the summary statement will identify the base used to determine the percentile. ND-designated applications still receive the assigned reviewers' written comments and scores on the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC) designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be designated Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC) by the SRG if it lacks significant and substantial merit; presents serious ethical problems in protection of human subjects; or presents serious ethical problems in the use of vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications designated NRFC do not proceed to the second level of peer review (Advisory Council/Board) because they cannot be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals grounds and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH peer review appeal system allows investigators and organizations to seek reconsideration if they believe the review process was flawed for reasons of bias of a reviewer, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the review outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This appeals policy does not apply to appeals of the technical evaluation of R&D contract projects, appeals of NIH funding decisions, or appeals of decisions concerning extensions of MERIT award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest management and declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: SROs document and manage conflicts of interest; reviewers must declare conflicts of interest with specific applications following NIH guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Managing Conflict of Interest in NIH Peer Review of Grants and Contracts for details; SROs ensure appropriate COI handling and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and integrity expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers receive access to grant applications approximately six weeks prior to the meeting and must maintain the confidentiality of peer review information. Applicants must not contact reviewers to influence review outcomes, send information directly to reviewers, or access review-related information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations by applicants have consequences; see Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers prepare a written critique for each application as directed by the SRO; assign numerical scores to each scored review criterion; make recommendations concerning scientific and technical merit, protections for human subjects, inclusion, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and appropriateness of budget requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should base critiques on review criteria and judgment of merit and follow SRO directions and NIH reviewer guidance documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SRG is led by an SRO who is the designated federal official responsible for ensuring that each application receives an objective and fair initial peer review and that applicable laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs analyze application content and completeness, document/manage conflicts of interest, recruit qualified reviewers (authority in field, dedication to fair reviews, collegiality, review experience, balanced representation), assign applications to reviewers, oversee regulatory aspects of meetings, and prepare summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for funding after dual review
rubrics_metrics.description: Only applications that are recommended for approval by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding; final funding decisions are made by the Institute/Center Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff consider overall impact scores, percentile rankings (if applicable), and summary statements in light of the IC's priorities when preparing funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Council Review for well-supported investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Council members conduct a Special Council Review of grant applications from investigators who currently receive $1 million or more in direct costs of NIH funding for Research Project Grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review determines if additional funds should be provided to already well-supported investigators and does not represent a cap on NIH funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review applicant options and next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: If not funded, applicants may resubmit addressing reviewer concerns or submit a new application; applicants receiving a summary statement are directed to Next Steps guidance and may contact their NIH program official for further advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is fundable, ICs may publish paylines; applicants should consult program officials for likelihood of funding and follow guidance from Grants Management Officers if an award is issued.
